facts.statement: Fukuisaurus remains were discovered in 1989 in Katsuyama, Fukui Prefecture, within rocks from the Barremian-aged Kitadani Formation.
facts.quote: Remains of Fukuisaurus were discovered in 1989, in Katsuyama, Fukui Prefecture, in rocks from the Kitadani Formation, dating to the Barremian.

facts.statement: The type species Fukuisaurus tetoriensis was described in 2003 by Yoshitsugu Kobayashi and Yoichi Azuma.
facts.quote: The type species, Fukuisaurus tetoriensis, was described in 2003 by Yoshitsugu Kobayashi and Yoichi Azuma.

facts.statement: Fukuisaurus was a relatively small ornithopod dinosaur.
facts.quote: Fukuisaurus was a relatively small ornithopod.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated Fukuisaurus to be 4.5 meters long and weigh 400 kg.
facts.quote: In 2010 Gregory S. Paul estimated its length at 4.5 meters and its weight at 400 kg.

facts.statement: Fukuisaurus was a bipedal animal capable of moving on four legs, with a build similar to Iguanodon, Ouranosaurus, and Altirhinus.
facts.quote: Being a bipedal, optionally quadrupedal, animal, it was similar in general build to Iguanodon, Ouranosaurus and Altirhinus.

facts.statement: According to its describers, Fukuisaurus had a non-kinetic skull where the maxilla was so fused to the vomer that sideways chewing was impossible.
facts.quote: According to the describers Fukuisaurus was exceptional in that its skull was not kinetic: the tooth-bearing maxilla would be so strongly fused to the vomer that a sideways chewing motion would have been impossible.

facts.statement: The describers assigned Fukuisaurus to Iguanodontia, but noted features suggesting it also belongs to Styracosterna.
facts.quote: Fukuisaurus was assigned by its describers to Iguanodontia, although the presence of a posterolateral process of the sternum indicated that it likely also belongs to Styracosterna.

facts.statement: There is a debate regarding Fukuisaurus's classification, with some studies placing it as a basal member of Hadrosauroidea and others recovering it as a non-hadrosauroid styracostern.
facts.quote: Ramírez-Velasco et al. (2012) found Fukuisaurus to be a basal member of Hadrosauroidea, while Bertozzo et al. (2017) recovered it as a non-hadrosauroid styracostern.

facts.statement: Fukuisaurus lived during the Aptian stage, between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Fukuisaurus is a genus of herbivorous ornithopod dinosaur that lived in Japan during the Early Cretaceous.
rejected.quote: Fukuisaurus (meaning "Fukui (Fortunate) lizard") is a genus of herbivorous ornithopod dinosaur that lived during the Early Cretaceous in what is now Japan.
